subject: Multiplex routing telemetry and SDK header request (Brightlane POC)
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multiplex routing telemetry and SDK header request (Brightlane POC)

Team —

Brightlane ran into a repeatable POC issue where requests routed to different runtime variants appear to be producing inconsistent outputs (they see a "variant_mismatch" error pattern in their client logs). They attached a small sample log (brightlane-error-log-20290615.txt).

As part of the investigation I think we should do two things:
1) Add a lightweight client-side header (example: "X-RW-Route-Hint: <route_hint>") that the SDK can set when an app wants deterministic routing for a session. The SDK can expose a new optional param on the request object (route_hint or route_preference).
2) Have the serving/runtime echo variant_id and route decision into telemetry/traces for request correlation (trace/span tag + log field). That will let us join Brightlane's client logs with runtime traces.

Ask: can runtime accept and surface a short header and expose variant_id consistently to logs/traces? Also: can the SDK team sketch the minimal API change and a fallback path so we don't break existing clients?

Why this matters: Brightlane is on the verge of converting a pilot to a paid deal and they observed nondeterministic behavior across retries. If we can give them a simple knob to force routing and correlate traces, we likely prevent churn.

Next steps I propose in-thread: Logan / Marissa: brief feasibility/cost estimate for runtime work. Karthik / Soojin: SDK API sketch + rollout plan (feature flagged). I can own coordination with Brightlane and HubSpot update.

Thanks,
Jonas
--
Jonas Weber
Lead, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: logan.wright@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiplex routing telemetry and SDK header request (Brightlane POC)

Jonas —

Thanks for the signal + logs. Quick thoughts from runtime side:

- Accepting a short header (X-RW-Route-Hint) is straightforward at the gateway layer; we can plumb it through request metadata into the routing decision.
- We should avoid coupling routing correctness to free-form strings; prefer a small enum or stable token: e.g. route_hint=preferred_variant:<variant-token> or route_hint=session_id:<client-sid>. Gateway can validate and forward.
- On the telemetry side we can start echoing a runtime field "variant_id" and include route_hint in the trace tags. That'll let a log join on (request_id, variant_id).

Estimate: prototype in gateway + runtime trace echo in ~3 dev-weeks (one engineer + one reviewer). We can make it behind a feature flag to avoid immediate rollout risk.

Temporary workaround: SDK can set a request-scoped client-side retry policy: if response contains variant_mismatch, mark session sticky to last-successful-variant for N minutes. That reduces churn while we build the proper hook.

I'll queue RW-3451 for initial scoping. Marissa — can you confirm if Brightlane needs the header to be set automatically by SDK or if they can add it manually for now?

—Logan
--
Logan Wright
Principal Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2029 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multiplex routing telemetry and SDK header request (Brightlane POC)

Jonas / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick look. Brightlane can temporarily patch the client to set a header; easiest for us is a request header that pins variant decisions for a session. The attached log shows repeated 502-like responses with a "variant_mismatch" token in our SDK wrapper and the client-side request id.

Our ask: if you can land a short-term gate that allows the SDK to set route_hint and for runtime to echo variant_id into traces within the next 2 weeks, we can proceed with the pilot conversion.

Two notes:
- We prefer route_hint to accept either a variant token or a session id.
- We need a minimal backwards-compatible path; if header absent, behaviour remains current.

Thanks,
Alex Huang
Engineering Manager, Brightlane

Quick plan and action items from Product/Customer success perspective:

1) Product position: we can support a simple header-based hint (X-RW-Route-Hint) that accepts two short forms: "variant:<token>" or "session:<sid>". This is an opt-in capability behind a console flag and SDK opt-in.
2) Runtime work: Logan to scope gateway accept + trace echo (RW-3451). Prioritize trace tag + log field for variant_id.
3) SDK work: Karthik to propose a minimal API change (new optional param on request: route_hint) and a client-side sticky fallback on variant_mismatch. SDK change should be feature-flagged and documented in release notes.
4) Rollout: behind feature flag with an initial customer-only enablement. No global default.

I've created the Jira ticket and linked the HubSpot deal (links below). I attached a trimmed trace snippet from Brightlane so runtime can see the request_id/ts pattern (route-trace-snippet.json).

Action owners & ETA:
- Logan: prototype + telemetry echo plan by 2029-07-03 (dev estimate 3w).
- Karthik: SDK API PR + integration tests by 2029-07-01.
- Soojin (Field): coordinate the Brightlane enablement and verify logs next week.

I'll update Brightlane after we have a rough ETA.

-Marissa
